page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Marginal notes in the right margin. Left edge: a strip of the neighbouring page, not transcribed.

main_text.p: stolas locum obtinet. Secundum Argumentū est, ꝙ rex Theodoricus & Episcoporum aliqui subscribentiū, utpote Augustinus Cantuariensis, & Mellitus Londoniensis (ipso attestāte{m} Baronio) tū tem-Tom. 8. pag.65.poris non fuerint inaugurati, qui propterea illam subscriptionem adjectitiam ingenuè fatetur; Tertiū erit, ꝙ datū sit anno ab Incarnatione Domini 594, q; dā-di formulam, etiā post tēpora Gregorij 7.inusitatam fuisse,ex eius Actis & Epistolis apparet. Quod autē tēpore Gregorij primi, Hispani ꝑ eras tantū, reliq; nationes ꝑ Indictiones coputarent, dostis notius est q, ut ulteriori aliqua probatione indigeat. Quartum, ꝙ Gregorius Septimus in sua ad Herimannū Episcopum Metense Epistola, ubi ex industria pro authoritate Pontificia supra Imperatoriā quicquid potuit conuassauit, huiꝰ tamē Priuilegij non omnino meminerit, licèt illi hoc affingat & Cæsar{n} Baronius in suis Annalibus, & {o}Seuerinus Binius, nota ad illam Epistolā marginali, utriq; fortassis decepti q ibidem ex alia eiusdem Gregorij Magni Epistola simile quid, citatis verbis illius Priuilegij allegetur: cū hoc ta-Tom. 8. pag 64.Ad epist. 21. Gregorij 7. Tom. 4.

page.notes: Left edge strip (neighbouring page) and show-through omitted. Superscript mark before "Baronio" read as m; mark after "Caesar" as n; mark before "Seuerinus" as o. Several abbreviations (q with flourish, p-with-stroke forms before "eras" and "Indictiones", "q;" before "decepti") are read by best judgement and may be doubtful. "conuassauit" is a doubtful reading. The last line "ta-" is read as a catchword, though it stands in the text block. Running head taken as "Lib. III. Scutum Regium.", with the number 205 at the top right.
